findings.evidence: No evals/ directory: neither evals/evals.json nor evals/trigger-queries.json exists under skills/ai-kit-session-wake.
findings.fix: Add evals/evals.json with at least three realistic prompts (casual, precise, one edge such as a live host at a usage limit), expected output, and verifiable assertions, plus evals/trigger-queries.json with about 20 queries (8-10 should-trigger, 8-10 should-not-trigger including near-misses such as a cross-AI hard-tier wait).

findings.evidence: A manual arm makes you own its done: an executor that later arms the same session sees refreshed, treats the wake as not its own and never closes it.
findings.fix: Name the follow-up: after a manual arm, the orchestrating session must run done itself when work ends, and must not treat a later executor refreshed line as that executor taking ownership.

findings.evidence: If the host cannot list jobs, create it on an arm that printed armed unconditionally. On a refreshed, create it only when the conversation holds no job-creation result for the same UTC time.
findings.fix: State one default: create the one-shot only on a line that starts with armed, and on refreshed create it only when no prior result in this conversation names the same UTC time, shim path and session id.

findings.evidence: Each Bash call starts a fresh shell, so re-substitute the value.
findings.fix: Drop the fresh-shell reminder; keep only the instruction to reuse the printed SHIM= path.

findings.evidence: Arm, Done and disarm, and Status and matrix are sequenced commands, but the skill never states the thinking check before arming by hand.
findings.fix: Add one line before Arm: before a manual arm, ask whether an executor already owns this session; if it does, do not arm.
